name: Aero
lede: Aero is a clear light blue first recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1920, in the years air travel itself was becoming a word for modern speed.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates Aero to 1920, plate 36, swatch H 6 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 lists it in block 186, among the grayish blues [1]. The name's link to aviation is not confirmed in the sources here, though the word and the decade line up [1].

In the color graph, Aero's closest neighbor is [[squill-blue]], 3.4 units away, with [[french-sky-blue]] and [[blue-jeans]] also near, and the basic term [[sky]] close behind at 4.5 [2]. [[baby-blue-eyes]], a separate library entry, sits 9.6 units off, paler and softer [2]. Munsell gives 2.2PB 7.2/7.7, a pale, moderately saturated blue [1]. The hex #7CB9E8 is a screen approximation; it is also a CSS Level 4 color keyword [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 18 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.08 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is Botticelli's *Mary Magdalene predella* (1425), five centuries before the name existed, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. The strongest later matches are skies and water, led by Frédéric Bazille's *The Western Ramparts at Aigues-Mortes* (1867) and Bernardo Bellotto's Venetian canal view, *The Campo di Santi Giovanni e Paolo* (1743) [3]. The 1800s carry the highest lift among centuries measured, about 1.7 times the base rate [3]. This is a computed color match on photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment test [3].
